message.content:
Here are some of the major airports in the United States, ranked by passenger traffic and overall importance:

| Airport | City | State | IATA Code | Notable Features |
|---------|------|-------|-----------|------------------|
| Hartsfield‑Jackson Atlanta International Airport | Atlanta | Georgia | ATL | Largest airport in the world by passenger traffic; major hub for Delta Air Lines. |
| Los Angeles International Airport | Los Angeles | California | LAX | Major gateway to Asia, Oceania, and Latin America; busiest in the Western U.S. |
| Chicago O’Hare International Airport | Chicago | Illinois | ORD | One of the oldest major hubs; key connecting point for domestic and international flights. |
| Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport | Dallas/Fort Worth | Texas | DFW | Largest airport in the U.S. by land area; major hub for American Airlines. |
| Denver International Airport | Denver | Colorado | DEN | Largest airport by land area in the U.S.; major hub for United Airlines and Southwest. |
| John F. Kennedy International Airport | New York City | New York | JFK | Major international gateway; primary hub for many carriers. |
| San Francisco International Airport | San Francisco | California | SFO | Key hub for transpacific flights; major focus city for United Airlines. |
| Seattle‑Tacoma International Airport | Seattle | Washington | SEA | Major hub for Alaska Airlines and a growing focus city for Delta. |
| Miami International Airport | Miami | Florida | MIA | Major hub for Latin American and Caribbean traffic; key for United and American. |
| Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport | Phoenix | Arizona | PHX | Major hub for Southwest Airlines; high passenger volume. |
| Orlando International Airport | Orlando | Florida | MCO | Major hub for leisure travel; primary focus city for Southwest. |
| Charlotte Douglas International Airport | Charlotte | North Carolina | CLT | Major hub for American Airlines; high domestic traffic. |
| Newark Liberty International Airport | Newark | New Jersey | EWR | Major hub for United Airlines; key gateway to the Northeast. |
| Washington Dulles International Airport | Washington, D.C. | Virginia | IAD | Major hub for United Airlines; important for government and business travel. |
| Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport | Detroit | Michigan | DTW | Major hub for Delta Air Lines; high domestic traffic. |
| Minneapolis‑Saint Paul International Airport | Minneapolis | Minnesota | MSP | Major hub for United Airlines; key for Midwest connectivity. |
| Boston Logan International Airport | Boston | Massachusetts | BOS | Major hub for Northeast traffic; key for JetBlue and Delta. |
| San Diego International Airport | San Diego | California | SAN | Growing hub for Southwest; important for West Coast and international flights. |
| Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport | Baltimore | Maryland | BWI | Major hub for Southwest; important for the Mid-Atlantic region. |
| Portland International Airport | Portland | Oregon | PDX | Major hub for Alaska Airlines; growing focus city for Southwest. |

These airports are among the busiest in terms of passenger numbers, flight operations, and connectivity, serving as critical hubs for both domestic and international travel across the United States.
